why: #26 published reaction numbers for five prints before any emitter existed. They are frozen here as an oracle: they pinned down the day-0 convention (base = last settled session STRICTLY BEFORE the print date) empirically, since anchoring on the print-date close instead reproduces none of the fourteen. Any future edit to the convention that changes these numbers is a silent regression, and --verify is what makes it loud.
convention: base = last session < print_date; dN = close N sessions after base; return = (close/base - 1) * 100
note_on_benchmark: The d5_vs_smh column is #26's own, which benchmarked EVERY print against SMH. The shipped emitter benchmarks against the per-name GROUP_PROXY (Jake's decision, 2026-08-27), so for DDOG (IGV) and RDDT (SPY) the DISPLAYED excess will differ from this column by design. SMH excess is asserted here anyway to prove the divergence is a deliberate benchmark change and not an arithmetic drift.
